Dear Dr Thomas,

Re: Mr Patrick Newton, aged 25 years

I am writing this letter to refer you Mr Newton, a 25-year-old accountant, whose features are suggestive of
inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Your diagnosis and assessment would be highly appreciated.

Regarding his social and medical history, he is a smoker and he has a six- month history of low-grade
intermittent joint pain and anxiety for which he has been managed accordingly. Moreover, he has a family      Comment [benchmark1]: Please note,
history of Crohn's disease.

Today, Mr Newton attended my surgery complaining of a 4 month history of mild diarrhea and low-grade          Comment [benchmark2]: 4-month
intermittent right lower quadrant abdominal pain associated with lethargy, anorexia and weight loss of 3
kg in the last 4 months. On examination, he was febrile. Although his abdomen showed generalised
tenderness, there were no hepato or splenomegaly. Furthermore, his FBE revealed increase in WBC.              Comment [benchmark3]: was
However, a decrease in both RBC and hemoglobin. In addition, his CPR and ESR were both elevated and his       Comment [benchmark4]: an
faecal occult blood test showed a positive result. Thus, he was consulted about his IBD and was advised on    Comment [benchmark5]: , but
smoking cessation.                                                                                            Comment [benchmark6]: both
                                                                                                              Comment [benchmark7]: counselled
In light of the above, I would be grateful if you could assess and manage his condition as you think          on
appropriate. If you have any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor
